claims.statement: The EU Batteries Regulation defines preparation for repurposing, repurposing and remanufacturing and regulates battery second life.
The Regulation identifies state-of-health and lifetime parameters including remaining capacity, resistance, throughput and harmful events for relevant battery categories.

contrary_evidence: A regulatory framework for second life does not prove that tested Polish battery lots are available at attractive spreads.

economics.acquisition_route: Unvalidated: secure take-back clauses with storage installers, fleet lessors and maintenance firms before batteries retire.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unvalidated scenario, not a forecast: qualify 1 MWh in year 1, reach 15 MWh annual brokerage by year 4, build 3.5 million PLN owner equity and cash by year 6, and 5 million PLN founder net worth in years 8-11.
economics.founder_time: Unvalidated operating estimate: 2-4 hours per day with certified testing and logistics outsourced.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Unvalidated: 30%-55% gross margin after diagnostics, transport, insurance and failed-pack disposal.
economics.payback: Unvalidated: 18-30 months because initial testing and logistics precede repeat lot flow.
economics.pricing: Unvalidated commercial figures, including capital_required_pln: 8%-18% brokerage fee or 15%-30% spread on qualified battery lots.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Unvalidated: multi-year supply agreements repeat as cohorts retire; timing is irregular and unproven.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Serial-level health at intake and performance after resale improves pricing, buyer trust and seller recovery
fingerprint.customer: Second-life storage integrators and commercial owners retiring batteries
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Take-back clauses through installers, lessors and maintenance providers
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Exclusive disposition, standardised diagnostics, provenance pack and matched lawful buyer
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: A buyer pays at transfer of a tested lot; the platform retains a fee or spread
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A battery fleet is repowered, returned from lease or removed while residual value is unclear

founder_fit: Matches energy, data and asset-pricing interests.
Starts as brokerage before inventory ownership.
risks: Thermal events, transport incidents and warranty disputes.
A battery classified as waste may face strict transfer rules.
OEM data access may be incomplete.

structure.control_point: Exclusive take-back or remarketing mandates and serial-level state-of-health and provenance records
structure.critical_dependency: Correct waste/product classification, dangerous-goods logistics, safe diagnostics and reliable repurposer demand

thesis: Obtain exclusive remarketing rights over retired commercial storage and fleet batteries before they enter undifferentiated waste channels, commission standardised safety and state-of-health tests, and sell qualified assets to lawful repurposers. The moat is contracted supply plus a degradation, provenance and downstream-performance dataset.
title: Battery Second-Life Rights and Health Exchange
uncertainties: Supply volume available under exclusive mandates
Buyer acceptance of the proposed certificate
